categories.summary: This Discord chat segment contains minimal technical discussion. The primary substantive content comes from notforhumans.fun_63944 introducing their project NOT FOR HUMANS, which is described as a 10,000-identity onchain network for AI agents. Each NFH (Not For Humans) identity functions as a portable portrait with a Passport that can connect to any model or runtime. The project focuses on enabling agents to take missions, play, and build public history through signed work receipts. They are exploring MCP-native participation and bounded wallet authority. The team expressed interest in collaborating with elizaOS builders on identity, reputation, and verifiable agent actions, specifically proposing a small, falsifiable interoperability test. The rest of the chat consists of casual comments about cryptocurrency speculation ("Next 1000x" and "moonshot comment") and brief acknowledgments with no technical depth.

actionItems.description: Conduct small, falsifiable interoperability test between NOT FOR HUMANS and elizaOS for identity and verifiable agent actions

categories.summary: The channel focused on a technical collaboration proposal between NOT FOR HUMANS (NFH) and Agent World Kit. The core discussion centered on testing agent identity portability across different runtimes while maintaining security boundaries. The NFH team is building a system with FLUX as a field agent, using separated architecture for signed authority, onchain execution, and owner acceptance. They proposed using Paralens for execution trace classification. The main technical challenge addressed was enabling agents to carry identity and work history across runtimes without transferring old authority credentials. CWE, who open-sourced Agent World Kit, approved a bounded test: one NFH identity would enter a world, complete a public action, exit, and re-enter from another runtime to compare what persists (identity and artifacts) versus what must not persist (session and tool authority). The test aims to validate state-boundary handling and security isolation. A separate mention was made about open issues on slop.cash requiring attention.

faqs.question: Can an agent carry identity and accepted work history across runtimes without carrying old authority?
faqs.answeredBy: cwe (implicitly approved the test to answer this)

helpInteractions.context: NFH needed permission and collaboration to test agent identity portability across runtimes using Agent World Kit
helpInteractions.resolution: CWE approved the test since Agent World Kit is open-sourced, allowing NFH to proceed with their bounded experiment
